claims.statement: The preselected logistic_regression/baseline recipe scored 0.9960 ROC-AUC on the once-consumed holdout (bootstrap 95% interval 0.9858–1.0000).
Do not promote features from importance alone; require decision-time availability, cross-fold stability, production availability, and monitoring.

decision_time_rule: Features must exist at the declared prediction moment; suspicious features require human semantic review.

evidence.production_feature_rule: A feature is a stronger candidate when it is decision-time available, stable across CV folds, contractually obtainable, monitored for missingness/drift, and not merely important in one fit.
evidence.selection_rule: Evaluate explicit dataset-specific parameter candidates on training CV; use the best tuned candidate only when mean ROC-AUC improves by at least 0.001, otherwise prefer baseline.

holdout_policy: Model and feature choices use training-only CV. The locked holdout is consumed only by optimization_reliability.
hypothesis: Conservative optimization and one final holdout evaluation will separate repeatable improvements from leaderboard noise.

required_outputs: identify missed leakage or validation risks
propose the smallest next experiment with a falsifiable success gate
cite experiment_id and evidence paths for every conclusion

challenges_to_claims.issue: The claim reports a strong holdout ROC-AUC, but the experiment question asks whether optimization produces a meaningful CV gain; the package does not include the baseline CV score, tuned CV score, or their uncertainty, so the optimization-gain part is unsupported.
Because the holdout is marked consumed, the reported holdout score should not be used as evidence for further model selection or iterative tuning without a fresh untouched evaluation set.
The recommendation is sensible, but it is not backed by explicit decision-time availability or production-availability evidence for the listed features in this package.
Cross-fold stability is based on only 3 observed folds, which is too sparse to support a strong stability conclusion.

review.decision: Do not claim a meaningful optimization gain from this package. Treat the holdout score as a consumed, one-time performance estimate only. Before any feature or recipe promotion, require a pre-registered comparison against the baseline on the same CV protocol and a decision-time/production-availability audit.
review.interpretation: The holdout result is strong predictive evidence for this dataset, but it does not by itself establish that optimization produced a meaningful gain. The package does not provide the baseline CV score, the tuned CV score, or their uncertainty, so the core question about optimization benefit remains unsupported. The feature-ranking note is directionally cautious, but any promotion decision still needs explicit decision-time and production-availability review; importance and 3-fold stability alone are insufficient to justify feature use.

next_experiment.hypothesis: If optimization truly improves the recipe, then the tuned candidate will exceed the baseline by at least 0.001 mean ROC-AUC under the same pre-registered CV protocol, and the improvement will persist under repeated/nested resampling.
next_experiment.success_gate: Pre-register the comparison; run paired nested or repeated CV on baseline and tuned candidate; declare optimization beneficial only if mean ROC-AUC improvement is >= 0.001 and the paired fold-wise difference is consistently positive across resamples. Do not touch the consumed holdout.
next_experiment.title: Paired baseline-vs-tuned nested CV with untouched holdout lock
next_experiment.why_smallest: This is the minimal falsifiable test that directly answers the optimization-gain question without reusing the consumed holdout or adding new modeling complexity.

observed_evidence.statement: The once-consumed holdout was evaluated and marked consumed.
The preselected logistic_regression/baseline recipe achieved holdout ROC-AUC 0.996031746031746 with bootstrap 95% interval [0.9857785443722944, 1.0].
The selection rule uses training CV and requires mean ROC-AUC improvement of at least 0.001 over baseline to prefer a tuned candidate.
The reported CV feature stability is based on 3 observed folds for the listed features.
The production feature rule requires decision-time availability, contractual obtainability, monitoring for missingness/drift, and stability across CV folds.

risks_and_missing_evidence: No baseline CV metric is shown, so the stated optimization threshold cannot be checked.
No tuned-candidate CV metric or fold-level distribution is shown, so any gain could be within noise.
The holdout is already consumed, so repeated model selection against it would risk leakage-by-iteration.
Only 3 CV folds are reported for feature stability, which is a weak basis for stability claims.
No decision-time availability evidence is provided for the top features.
No production contract, lineage, or monitoring evidence is provided for the top features.
No calibration or threshold-selection protocol is shown for the holdout classification metrics.
No nested-CV or repeated-CV evidence is shown to assess optimization reliability.

question: Does optimization produce a meaningful CV gain, and how does the preselected recipe perform on the once-consumed holdout?
